1	# AlgebraicJacobian (rebuild)
2	
3	<!-- archon:readme -->
4	
5	## Project
6	
7	A **from-scratch rebuild** of the Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization of the **Jacobian of a smooth,
8	proper, geometrically irreducible curve** over a field (Christian Merten's AI challenge, inspired by
9	Kevin Buzzard's Riemann-surface version). By a smooth curve we mean a geometrically irreducible,
10	smooth scheme of relative dimension one over a field.
11	
12	This project supplies the missing definitions (`genus`, `Jacobian`, the Abel–Jacobi map `ofCurve`)
13	and theorems (the Jacobian is smooth of relative dimension equal to the genus, proper, geometrically
14	irreducible, and is the Albanese variety of the curve, characterized by the universal property
15	`exists_unique_ofCurve_comp`). It targets the **extended** challenge: additionally, the Jacobian is
16	**functorial** in the curve (`Jacobian.functor`) and **commutes with base change of fields**
17	(`baseChangeIso` with identity and cocycle coherences, and Abel–Jacobi compatibility
18	`baseChange_ofCurve`), which makes the construction canonical.
19	
20	It is rebuilt rather than continued: the goal is a cleaner, more general, mathlib-idiomatic
21	infrastructure and a shorter, clearer path to the conclusion. The existing project
22	`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` may be **read** when genuinely blocked, but nothing is

1	# LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon
2	
3	LeanAG Horizon is a multi-project Lean 4 and Mathlib workspace for formalizing algebraic
4	geometry with [Archon Horizon](https://github.com/frenzymath/Archon-Horizon). Its central goal is
5	the algebraic-geometry version of the [Algebraic Jacobian challenge](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian.20challenge/near/587802685),
6	proposed by Christian Merten after Kevin Buzzard's differential-geometry challenge.
7	
8	> [!IMPORTANT]
9	> The workspace develops **two live routes** to the Algebraic Jacobian challenge. Follow the
10	> project named by the active task rather than treating either route as reference-only.
11	>
12	> - `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` continues the ambitious Picard-scheme route, building
13	>   representability by the Milne–Kollár construction of `Pic^r`, then `Pic^0` and the Albanese
14	>   property. Its Grassmannian, graded-algebra and flattening-stratification substrate is sorry-free
15	>   and still consumed, but the Quot-scheme endgame it was first written for is not the path being
16	>   built. Since 2026-07-28 its headline is stated over an arbitrary base field, with
17	>   representability asked of the étale-sheafified Picard functor and no rational-point hypothesis.
18	> - `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` develops a cleaner curve-specialized route
19	>   from protected target statements.
20	
21	The two projects share mathematical sources and supporting subprojects while keeping independent
22	Lean roots, blueprints, and roadmaps. The rebuild is listed first in the workspace manifest as the
23	default project; explicitly scoped tasks may and do advance the ambitious original route.
24	
25	The [live dashboard](https://axeldlv00.github.io/LeanAlgebraicGeometry/) is the best view of current
26	tasks, commits, session logs, blueprint graphs, and declaration-level progress. A static snapshot
27	is published approximately every 30 minutes; GitHub Pages deployment and caching can add a few
28	minutes before a new snapshot is visible.
29	
30	## Repository Layout
31	
32	| Path | Role |
33	| --- | --- |
34	| `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` | Cleaner curve-specialized AJC route and workspace default. |
35	| `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` | Ambitious Picard-scheme AJC route (Milne–Kollár representability), maintained by scoped tasks. |
36	| `SubProjects/` | Supporting, extracted, and related-paper formalizations available to the active project. |
37	| `references/` | Shared mathematical sources and retrieval notes. |
38	| `.archon-horizon/` | Workspace state: tasks, roadmap, inbox, run metadata, graphs, and ledger. |
39	| `config.yaml` | Ordered workspace manifest. The rebuild is listed first because it is the primary project. |
40	
41	Each route has its own overview:
42	
43	- [`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/README.md`](MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/README.md)
44	- [`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/README.md`](MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/README.md)
45

47	
48	The workspace currently registers these projects, in priority order:
49	
50	| Project | Purpose |
51	| --- | --- |
52	| **`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`** | Cleaner curve-specialized route; default project in the workspace manifest. |
53	| `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` | Ambitious Picard-scheme, `Pic^0`, and Albanese route. |
54	| `Line-Bundle-Comparison-Iso` | Extracted line-bundle pullback, tensor, and dual comparison infrastructure. |
55	| `Albanese` | Albanese universal property, rigidity, and rational-map-extension infrastructure. |
56	| `Cech-Cohomology` | Čech computation of higher direct images and its cohomological substrate. |
57	| `GR-Quot-Closure` | Relative Grassmannian and quotient-representability infrastructure. |
58	| `MR0555258-Compactifying-Picard` | Compactifying the Picard scheme (D'Souza), under `SubProjects/RelatedPapersFormalisation/`. |
59	| `Picard-IdentityComponent` | Extracted Picard identity-component and `Pic^0` development. |
60	
61	These member projects remain useful sources of proved APIs, mathematical designs, and failure
62	memory for both main routes.
63	
64	## Working in a Main Project
65	
66	The workspace currently uses Lean and Mathlib `v4.31.0`. Build the project named by the task. For
67	the ambitious Picard-scheme route:
68	
69	```bash
70	cd MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge
71	lake build
72	```
73	
74	The rebuild uses the shared workspace package directory at `.lake-packages`, so member projects
75	can reuse the same Mathlib checkout while retaining independent build directories.
76	
77	For workspace-wide exploration, run commands from the repository root:
78	
79	```bash
80	horizon dashboard
81	horizon graph -p Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge frontier
82	horizon search "Jacobian Picard representability"
83	```
84	
85	The first command starts the local dashboard. The graph command shows the ranked proof frontier
86	for the active project, and search queries declarations across the workspace and Mathlib.
87	
88	Treat `graph frontier` output as advisory and verify each row in the tree: neither main project has
89	an `hgraph/config.yaml`, so `horizon graph … sync` is a no-op and the stored graph drifts behind
90	landed work. Tracked in inbox `I-0501` (missing config) and `I-0472` (the scanner also invents
91	declarations from docstring prose).
92	
93	## Methodology
94	
95	[Archon Horizon](https://github.com/frenzymath/Archon-Horizon) coordinates long-running
96	formalization while keeping mathematical and operational state explicit:
97	
98	- **Horizon sessions** implement and verify Lean proofs against concrete tasks.
99	- **Fresh-context reviewers** such as Ground, work-reviewer, and janitor are dispatched at review
100	  and maintenance checkpoints rather than acting as a permanent second driver.
101	- **Blueprint graphs (`hgraph`)** track declaration dependencies, proof status, comments, and the
102	  ranked frontier for each project.
103	- **Roadmap, tasks, and inbox** record strategy, scoped work, cross-session handoffs, and durable
104	  failure memory.
105	- **The workspace ledger** records coherent commits and powers the public dashboard's progress
106	  and session views.
107	
108	Concurrent sessions can share a project's root import file. When adding one
109	import, build the staged root from the ledger's current `HEAD` and insert only
110	that line; do not stage the whole on-disk root, which may contain another
111	session's uncommitted imports.
112	
113	The mathematical blueprint is kept separate from implementation journals. Lean-specific progress
114	and failed approaches belong in graph comments, tasks, or the inbox, while the blueprint remains a
115	timeless account of the mathematics.
116	
117	## Contributing
118	
119	Contributions are welcome, but keep the two routes and task scope explicit:
120	
121	- **AJC proofs and infrastructure:** change only the main project named by the task; share reusable
122	  inputs through the supporting projects when appropriate.
123	- **Protected statements:** do not alter the signatures in the rebuild's `Challenge.lean` or files
124	  covered by `archon-protected.yaml` without prior agreement. Contributions should discharge those
125	  statements, not weaken or reshape them silently.
126	- **Issues and discussions:** include the declaration name and file path, and state whether the
127	  question concerns the statement, naming, proof strategy, or intended use.
128	- **Large changes:** check the live dashboard or open an issue first so work does not duplicate an
129	  active Horizon task.
130	- **Supporting work:** a focused subproject under `SubProjects/` is appropriate when a reusable
131	  dependency needs to be developed independently, but its intended consumer should be the active
132	  rebuild.
133	
134	Clear, stable, mathematical declaration names and warning-free builds are expected. Using the

136	blueprint graph, and ledger conventions.
